title: Dynamic-programming values and acceptance probability
statement: Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $x$ be a finite bit string, and let $s,V,t$ be natural numbers. Suppose there is a function $sp:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ such that on every input and every choice string, the total number of work-tape cells visited by $N$ is at most $sp$ of the input length; suppose also that $sp(|x|)\le s$ and $2^{K( s+\ell(|x|)+1)}\le V$, where $K$ is the configuration-code constant of $N$ and $\ell(n)=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor+1$. For every natural number $t$ and every choice string $v$, the depth-$t$ dynamic-programming value at the code of the configuration reached after choices $v$, viewed as a rational number, equals $2^t$ times the probability that the machine, after choices $v$ followed by a uniformly random Boolean string of length $t$, is halted and has output exactly the one-bit string $[1]$.
hypotheses_covered: N uses at most sp(n) work-tape cells on every input and choice string
